audits.summary: Mixed feasibility, skewing toward PARTIAL/GAP. The real apex-gtm-api (production tree on branch release/go-live-2026-06-01, NOT the local master checkout whose packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma is the legacy pre-go-live version) has the data substrate for ~half of these tiles but exposes NONE of the five dashboard routes — they are all net-new BFF aggregations. Confirmed-real prisma models (from .swarm-out snapshots + EvidenceLedgerService + gdpr-erasure MANIFEST org-cascade list): GraphRun, OutreachArtifact (status enum DRAFT/PENDING_REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED/SENT/SUPPRESSED), EvidenceEvent (append-only: orgId/runId/traceId/kind/refType/refId/payload/createdAt), MeetingLedger, LeadScore, Person/Company (lead engine), IcpProfile. Biggest gaps: (1) NO Notification model, NO NotificationPreference model — both /notifications endpoints are full gaps with no DB backing; (2) Org has NO welcomeComplete/currentStep column (only a POST /api/signup/onboarding/complete side-effect that seeds ICP+integrations+agent) — /welcome/status cannot read true state; (3) /activity expects per-agent rows (agentName/agentType/action/stage) but the only real event stream is EvidenceEvent whose schema is kind/refType/refId/payload — heavy lossy transform, and agentName/Type/stage must be SYNTHESIZED from kind; (4) /today/kpis: artifactsPending/SentToday are real via OutreachArtifact, replyRate7d + qualifiedMeetingsBooked have NO query path (no Conversation model at all; MeetingLedger exists but no service/route queries it and only PROPOSED rows are written), leadsSourced/Scored map to Person/LeadScore. Auth: all real routes are org-scoped by OrgScopeGuard (Clerk JWT org_id claim cross-checked against x-org-id header; dev falls back to trusting x-org-id). The mock hardcodes ORG_ID="org_mynoted" and must be replaced by the authenticated org. No real route under /today, /activity, /notifications, /welcome exists today; the BFF must own all aggregation + the synthetic/persisted state for notifications and welcome.

endpoints.real_source: OutreachArtifact (prisma.outreachArtifact — status enum + sentAt/createdAt, org-scoped) backs artifactsPending (status=PENDING_REVIEW count) and artifactsSentToday (status=SENT, sentAt>=todayStart). Person/Company lead-engine tables back leadsSourcedToday (Person.createdAt>=todayStart via company join) and LeadScore backs leadsScored (count where score not null). replyRate7d: NONE (no Conversation/inbound-reply model in prod schema; EvidenceEvent has messageSent but no reply.received kind). qualifiedMeetingsBooked: MeetingLedger model exists in prod schema but has NO service/controller/query path and only PROPOSED rows are ever written — effectively NONE. No real route exists; nearest service symbols: OutreachArtifactsService (apps/api/src/outreach), LeadsService, GraphService.
endpoints.transform: BFF computes 6 counts in parallel scoped to authenticated orgId. artifactsPending=count(OutreachArtifact status=PENDING_REVIEW); artifactsSentToday=count(status=SENT, sentAt>=startOfDay); leadsSourcedToday=count(Person joined to Company.orgId, createdAt>=startOfDay); leadsScored=count(LeadScore where qualifiedAt!=null OR score>0). replyRate7d -> hardcode 0 / null until an inbound-reply source exists. qualifiedMeetingsBooked -> count(MeetingLedger where status in {PROPOSED,...}) IF a query path is added, else 0. Mock's conversationsTable-based reply/meeting math has no real equivalent and must be dropped. Output keys exactly: artifactsPending, artifactsSentToday, replyRate7d, qualifiedMeetingsBooked, leadsSourcedToday, leadsScored.
endpoints.notes: Org-scoping mandatory: replace mock ORG_ID="org_mynoted" with orgId from OrgScopeGuard (req.orgId / Clerk org_id). Read-only, no write-path safety needed. Two of six tiles (replyRate7d, qualifiedMeetingsBooked) are GAPS — surface as 0 or omit; do not fabricate. Today-boundary must respect org timezone (Org has no timezone column in legacy schema — prod OrgSettings/timezone needed; otherwise UTC). No pagination.

endpoints.real_source: EvidenceEvent table (EvidenceLedgerService.append -> prisma.evidenceEvent; columns orgId, runId, traceId, kind, refType, refId, payload JSON, createdAt; append-only trigger live on apex-prod-db since 2026-05-24). EVIDENCE_EVENT_KIND has lead.sourced/lead.scored/message.drafted/qa.pass/qa.fail/approval.requested/approval.granted/approval.denied/artifact.persisted/message.sent/crm.synced/tenant.deletion. No real GET route exists; secondary candidate is GraphRun rows (GraphService.listGraphRuns) for run-level entries. The mock's activityEventsTable (agentName/agentType/action/stage columns) does NOT exist in the real schema.
endpoints.transform: Heavy lossy transform. BFF reads EvidenceEvent for orgId ordered by createdAt desc, take=limit, then maps each event to ActivityEvent: id=evidenceEvent.id; timestamp=createdAt.toISOString(); action/stage/agentType/agentName must be SYNTHESIZED from kind via a lookup table (e.g. lead.sourced->agentType 'sdr'/stage 'sourcing'/action 'Sourced N leads'; message.drafted->'sdr'/'drafting'; approval.requested->'pipeline'/'approving'; message.sent->'sdr'/'sending'; qa.*->'reply' or 'pipeline'); artifactId=refId when refType='outreach_artifact' else null; leadId=refId when refType='person' else null. The mock's filter buckets (outbound/pipeline/conversations/all) map to sets of synthesized stages, applied in-memory after the synth step. agentName is not stored anywhere — synthesize a stable display name per agentType.
endpoints.notes: Org-scoped via EvidenceEvent.orgId; honor OrgScopeGuard orgId not mock ORG_ID. Read-only. agentName/agentType/action/stage are NOT real columns — they are derived, so the 'agent-level' fidelity the FE expects is approximate. Pagination is take=limit only (no page/total). EVIDENCE_LEDGER_ENABLED!=false gate means events only exist when enabled in prod. Consider unioning GraphRun lifecycle rows for richer pipeline entries.

audits.summary: PARTIAL overall. The real backend has a genuine artifacts domain — module apps/api/src/outreach (OutreachArtifactsController + OutreachArtifactsService) over prisma model OutreachArtifact (packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma, live in prod since 2026-05-22). NOTE: the canonical go-live source is NOT the master checkout at "/Users/nikhil/Desktop/apex v3-frontend + backend/apex-product" (that apps/api/src is the LEGACY codebase with no outreach/ module and a schema.prisma lacking OutreachArtifact); the real code is at "/Users/nikhil/Desktop/apex-product/apex-product/apps/api/src/outreach". Core read/approve/reject map well, but FOUR structural gaps make the contract only partial: (1) routes differ — real routes are GET/POST /api/outreach-artifacts[/:id][/approve|/reject] (global prefix "api"), not /artifacts; the openapi /artifacts/* paths must be re-mapped by the BFF. (2) The OpenAPI OutreachArtifact response shape is much richer than the DB row: structured recipient{name,email,title,company}, citations[], evaluatorScores{pii,hallucination,citationCoverage,toxicity}, sendPolicy{...}, cohort, approvedAt/sentAt — none of these exist as first-class columns. recipient is only a recipientRef string; citations live inside payload.brief_facts (SDR rows only); evaluatorScores are posted to LangSmith as fire-and-forget feedback, NOT persisted in Postgres (HARD GAP); sendPolicy is environment-driven (OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS, fail-closed) not per-row; cohort does not exist. (3) Enum mismatch: DB OutreachArtifactStatus is DRAFT/PENDING_REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED/SENT — there is NO SUPPRESSED state, and no suppression/do-not-contact model exists at all. (4) Three of seven endpoints have NO real route: GET /artifacts/pending, POST /artifacts/{id}/suppress, POST /artifacts/bulk-approve are NONE. Also list has no pagination (hardcoded take:100/no offset) and approve/reject REQUIRE a reviewedBy body field the FE never sends. Auth is Clerk JWT via OrgScopeGuard with org derived from the verified org_id claim (x-org-id dev header only when ALLOW_DEV_ORG_HEADER=true and NODE_ENV!=production); all queries are already org-scoped. Write-path safety (dry-run/fail-closed) is preserved automatically: approve only enqueues to OutreachSendQueueService and the SendOutreachWorker forces a mock send unless the org is in OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS (today tenant-zero only).

BFF must: (1) name = `${firstName} ${lastName}`; (2) email = bestEmail (EmailCandidate w/ highest confidence); (3) company = company.name, domain = companyDomain; (4) score = LeadScore.score (real range 0..~155, threshold 100 = qualified) -> FE expects 0..100-ish int, may need clamp/normalize; (5) stage = SYNTHESIZE from qualifiedAt/score (no real `stage` column) ; (6) cohort A|B = SYNTHESIZE (no real field; could derive from score band); (7) emailStatus DELIVERABLE|HIGH_PROBABILITY|CATCH_ALL = map from EmailCandidate.verificationResult (VALID->DELIVERABLE, CATCH_ALL->CATCH_ALL, else HIGH_PROBABILITY); (8) intentSignals[{label,confidence}] = map from Company.intentSignals (String[]) -> needs a confidence (Company.intentScore is a single int, not per-signal) so confidence must be synthesized; (9) sendPolicy = DERIVE from Org-level live-send/postal/unsubscribe + suppression (no per-lead column) ; (10) geo/country/industry/headcountEstimate = Company.country/industry/employeeRange (companyLogoUrl/avatarUrl = NONE); lastContactedAt = NONE (no per-person contact timestamp in schema).

Pagination: real listPeople supports page/limit (limit capped 100) — matches FE page/limit defaults 1/25. FILTER GAPS: real endpoint supports seniority/department/minScore only; FE filters stage/intentSignal/geo/cohort/industry/q(search)/sort are NOT supported server-side — BFF must either translate (geo->Company.country, industry->Company.industry via a custom Prisma where) or filter in-memory after fetch (breaks pagination totals). `q` free-text search and `sort` are unimplemented. audits.summary: PARTIAL overall, leaning toward heavy BFF work + one hard gap. The real apex-gtm-api has NO flat `Lead` entity: a lead is a composite of Person + Company + LeadScore + EmailCandidate (+ EvidenceEvent for detail), org-scoped through Person.company.orgId / LeadScore.orgId. The active master checkout exposes GET /leads/people and /leads/people/:id (not /leads), so the BFF must rename the route and assemble/synthesize most FE fields. (1) GET /leads — partial: composite assembly + name/email/company mapping is doable, but stage, cohort(A|B), emailStatus, per-signal intent confidence, sendPolicy, lastContactedAt, logos/avatars are SYNTHESIZED or NONE, and the FE filters stage/intentSignal/geo/cohort/industry/q/sort are unsupported server-side (only seniority/department/minScore exist) — geo/industry can be translated to Company.country/industry, the rest need in-memory filtering that breaks pagination totals. (2) GET /leads/{id} — partial: Person detail maps, but scoreBreakdown{fit,intent,engagement,timing} must be lossy-rebucketed from the real flat point-attribution breakdown, and researchBrief is not persisted as a queryable field (briefs are transient inside the SDR subgraph). (3) POST /leads/{id}/trigger-outbound — partial + granularity mismatch: no per-lead route; closest is GraphService.runPipelineGraph(orgId, icpProfileIds[]) (org/ICP-cohort scoped, BullMQ-enqueued, 409 single-flight guard) with no HTTP controller in this checkout — and the dry-run/fail-closed + OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS=tenant-zero gating MUST be preserved. (4) POST /leads/bulk-suppress — GAP: no suppression model/route exists in master's Prisma schema; needs a new SuppressedRecipient table + endpoint + wiring into the send-policy guard, applied via the DB safety workflow. GAP-DOMINANT. The conversations/inbox domain has essentially no persistence layer in the real apex-gtm-api. The local Prisma schema (packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma, 442 lines: Org, User, AgentTemplate, Agent, Integration, AgentRun, AgentLog, RunStep, AgentMemory, IcpProfile, Company, Person, EmailCandidate, PatternStore, LeadScore, ScrapeJob) contains NO Conversation, ConversationMessage, InboundEmail, Reply, Thread, or sentiment model. There is NO /conversations controller anywhere in apps/api/src (controllers: auth, hubspot, leads, runtime, agents, health, signup, integrations, orgs, runs, gmail, linkedin, billing). The only inbound-email capability is a live Gmail-API passthrough — GmailService.listMessages/getMessage/getThread/searchMessages in apps/api/src/integrations/gmail/gmail.service.ts (returns GmailMessage{id,threadId,snippet,from,to,subject,date,labelIds,body}) — which is NOT a persisted conversation store, has no sentiment/needsReply/archived/unread flags, no reply-intelligence, requires a CONNECTED Gmail Integration row with encrypted OAuth tokens per org, and is scoped by ?orgId= query param (not the Clerk session). The reply-handler agent template (apps/api/src/agents/templates/reply-handler.template.ts) DEFINES intent classification (INTERESTED/OBJECTION/NOT_NOW/UNSUBSCRIBE/etc.) and contextual reply drafting as a system prompt, but those outputs are not written to any conversation/sentiment table. NOTE the memory references to a Gmail Pub/Sub inbound-push handler (rev 0079) and Phase-2.5 prod tables (OutreachArtifact/GraphRun/MeetingLedger) are NOT present in this local checkout — even those would not supply conversation threads, sentiment, or archive state. Net: list/get can be PARTIALLY faked from Gmail threads only when Gmail is connected and only for tenant-zero; draft-reply can map to a run trigger; archive has no backing store and is a hard gap. To productionize, the BFF (or backend) must introduce a Conversation + ConversationMessage + ReplyIntelligence persistence layer plus an inbound-sync + sentiment-classification pipeline — none of which exists today.

audits.summary: Mostly FEASIBLE but split across two backend lineages. The FE contract is named after the DEPLOYED apex-gtm-api LangGraph model `prisma.graphRun` (RUNNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL/COMPLETED/FAILED enum is an exact match) served by GraphService.listGraphRuns/getGraphRun/runPipelineGraph (confirmed in .swarm-out/langsmith-runtree-parent/apps/api/src/graph/graph.service.ts). This checkout (apps/api) is the LEGACY lineage and only carries `AgentRun` + `Agent`/`AgentTemplate`; the graph module, the GraphRun controller, and the GraphRun prisma model are NOT in this tree (live only in the release/go-live worktree, not mounted here). BIGGEST GAPS: (1) GraphRun has NO aggregate metric columns — leadsSourced, artifactsGenerated, agentsInvolved, costUsd, durationMs, triggeredBy, completedAt do not exist on the row; every one of these must be DERIVED by the BFF from the EvidenceEvent ledger (kinds in .swarm-out/gdpr-erasure/apps/api/src/observability/evidence-event.types.ts, refType='graph_run') and from startedAt vs status-transition time. (2) The /agents roster the FE wants (sdr/content/reply/reporting with live activity sparklines) does NOT map to the real `Agent` table (which is org-configured SALES/MARKETING/OPS agents); it maps to FIXED LangGraph node identities + EvidenceEvent activity, exactly like the mock's hardcoded AGENT_DEFINITIONS — so /agents is a synthetic/derived view, a partial. (3) Org scoping must come from the Clerk-authenticated session in the BFF; the legacy controllers pass orgId as an unauthenticated query param which must NOT be exposed. (4) Known envelope mismatch (MEMORY graph-runs-envelope-mismatch): deployed listGraphRuns returns a bare GraphRun[] array, but FE wants {items,total,page,limit} — BFF must wrap + paginate. (5) Write-path /runs/trigger: real runPipelineGraph REQUIRES icpProfileIds and enforces single-flight (ConflictException if a run is RUNNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL); FE sends an empty body, so BFF must resolve org default ICP profile(s) and surface 409. Dry-run/fail-closed outreach default is preserved downstream by the graph itself (OUTREACH_LIVE_FOR_ORGS gate), not by this endpoint.

audits.summary: PARTIAL/MOSTLY-GAP. The real apex-product/apps/api backend covers only ~3 of the 12 settings concerns with real models+routes: org identity (Org model + GET/PATCH /orgs/:id), integrations (Integration model + full OAuth connect/disconnect + catalog), and billing (Razorpay subscription). Everything compliance- and configuration-related that this premium FE assumes is MISSING from the real backend: there is NO model/route for org compliance state (liveSendEnabled, postalAddress, unsubscribeUrl, suppression list, allowlisted domains), NO cadence model, NO styleConfig (brand voice) model, NO team-invite flow (only Clerk-webhook-driven User rows), NO multi-key ApiKey model (only a single User.apiKey string), and NO notificationPrefs model. The Org model itself also lacks most fields the OrgSettings schema requires (logoUrl, timezone, senderName, creditsRemaining, welcomeComplete; plan is an enum TRIAL|STARTER|GROWTH|ENTERPRISE not a free string; UpdateOrgDto only permits name+plan). IcpProfile exists but with substantially different field names (targetTitles/targetIndustries/targetGeos/minEmployees/maxEmployees/techStackSignals/intentKeywords vs FE titles/industries/geos/sizeBand/intentSignals/exclusionDomains) and is keyed by name with a 1:many relation, not the singleton the FE assumes. Biggest gaps: org compliance/health, cadence, style, team invite/remove, api-keys CRUD, notifications — all require NEW Prisma models + NestJS modules before the BFF can be more than a thin mock pass-through. Multi-tenant note: the mock hardcodes ORG_ID='org_mynoted'; the real API derives orgId from the Clerk JWT via OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/common/org-scope.guard.ts) and requires it on header/query/body, so the BFF must inject the authenticated orgId on every call.

VERIFICATION = Clerk RS256 JWT, verified in-process (no Clerk SDK, no session cookies). Source of truth:

GUARD: `apps/api/src/common/org-scope.guard.ts` `OrgScopeGuard`, registered GLOBALLY as `APP_GUARD` in `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` (lines 33-38). On every request (unless `@SkipOrgGuard()`):
  1. extractOrgId() reads orgId from `x-org-id` header, then `?orgId=` query, then body.orgId. If NONE present → `return false` (deny by default).
  2. If Clerk enabled (any of `CLERK_DOMAIN` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` / `CLERK_JWKS_URL` set): requires `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, verifies via `verifyClerkToken()`.
  3. Requires `payload.org_id` claim AND `payload.org_id === orgId` (the requested org) else `ForbiddenException`. Stashes `req.clerkUserId = payload.sub`, `req.clerkOrgId`, `req.orgId`.
  4. Confirms org exists in DB (`prisma.org.findUnique`).
  Local-dev fallback: if NO Clerk env is set, JWT check is SKIPPED and it TRUSTS the raw `x-org-id` header — must NOT happen in prod (prod has Clerk env set, so verification is live).

JWT MECHANICS: `apps/api/src/common/jwt.util.ts` `verifyClerkToken()` — fetches Clerk JWKS (`https://<domain>/.well-known/jwks.json`, domain derived from `CLERK_JWKS_URL` or decoded from the `pk_` publishable key), caches keys 24h, verifies RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 via WebCrypto, checks `exp`. Payload type expects `sub`, `org_id?`, `org_role?`, `email?`.

CRITICAL BFF CONSEQUENCE — the org-scope contradiction: the canonical workhorse-os FE deliberately NEVER sends `x-org-id` (http-client.ts line 9-10, leads-api.ts, api-client.ts comment "never sends x-org-id… backend derives org scope from the verified JWT org_id"). BUT the LOCAL master guard extractOrgId() DENIES (returns false) when no orgId is present in header/query/body — it only cross-checks, it does NOT derive orgId from the JWT by itself. So either (a) prod's release/go-live-2026-06-01 guard was changed to derive orgId from the JWT (likely, since the canonical FE works against prod), or (b) the canonical client actually relies on a prod-only behavior. The BFF MUST resolve this explicitly: simplest + safe option = the BFF reads the verified Clerk `org_id` (it can decode/verify the same JWT, jwt.util is reusable) and SETS `x-org-id` itself when forwarding to apex-gtm-api, so it works against BOTH master and release behavior. Never trust an `x-org-id` supplied by the browser.
